## 2776235f38d3

**Reproduced defect: canonical-support and shortcut failure.**  Audited generator
SHA-256:
`c6d48140ec42ffd76ec6a33954ebd577dac3aa9844a32997a97337e2a3d22097`.
The generator has no pinned `RULE_HASH`; the selected Racket source used by the
probe has rule hash `2ab573211d3b`.

The generator hard-codes “exactly one color-7 ignored noise cell.”  Its own
`self_check` therefore rejects all five canonical inputs:

- train 0 has three color-7 distractor cells;
- train 1 uses four color-6 distractor cells;
- train 2 uses four color-5 distractor cells;
- train 3 uses three color-8 distractor cells; and
- test 0 uses four color-9 distractor cells.

An independent XOR oracle matches all five canonical labels, so the rejection is
not caused by the canonical rule.  A concrete rival—apply normalized XOR only
when the input has exactly one color-7 cell, otherwise return blank—matches
300/300 generated defaults across easy/medium/hard because every sampled input
has exactly one color-7 cell, yet fails all 5 canonical pairs.  Thus generated
data teaches a noncanonical color identity restriction.

Minimal reproducer files:

- `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/input.json` — canonical train pair 1 input with
  color-6 distractors;
- `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/canonical_expected.json` — canonical expected output;
- `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/rival.json` — the shortcut's blank output;
- `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/racket.json` — selected authority output `[[8]]` and
  source bindings; and
- `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/probe.json` — all canonical/sample/override counts.

Additional contract defect: a request for eight advertised overrides produced a
grid byte-identical to the baseline, and an unknown override was silently
accepted.  The strict override audit retained more than 40,000 findings under
`checks/audit/2776235f38d3-override/`; lint also reports the missing rule pin.
The combined audit's semantic stage failed because no executable semantic
contract was declared.  This was an audit-only target and was intentionally not
modified.

## 2776235f38d3

**Reproduced defect at generator SHA-256 `c6d48140ec42ffd76ec6a33954ebd577dac3aa9844a32997a97337e2a3d22097`.** The task's intended operation is normalized XOR over the two relevant colored objects while ignoring distractors. The current generator and validator collapse that domain to exactly one color-7 distractor. All 5 canonical inputs are rejected by `self_check`: the first contains three color-7 cells, and the other four use distractor colors 6, 5, 8, and 9 rather than color 7.

A plausible shortcut—“apply normalized XOR only when there is exactly one color-7 cell; otherwise output blank”—matches 30/30 generated inputs and 30/30 selected-Racket outputs across 10 seeds in each difficulty band. It fails canonical pair 1, whose exact input is `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/input.json`: the distractor is color 6, the independent oracle and selected Racket both output `[[8]]`, while the shortcut outputs `[[0]]`. That input fails the current validator with `expected exactly one color-7 ignored noise cell, found 0`, so it is canonical-lawful but outside the documented generated domain.

Evidence and reproduction: `checks/audit/2776235f38d3/probe.json`, `oracle.json`, `rival.json`, `racket.json`, `generated-inputs.json`, and `generated-racket.json`. The independent probe matched all 5 canonical labels, and the Racket receipt records executed rule hash `2ab573211d3b`. No source was changed; audit-only finding.
